claims_supported: Mixed Armistice Commission majority found a major, unprovoked and premeditated Israeli regular-army attack on Jordanian territory near Husan on 25–26 September; records 12 National Guards killed near Husan, two civilians wounded, attack at Wadi Fukin and school demolition, plus additional losses at Sharafa police post and Khader village

title: Israelis destroy Jordanian stronghold in seven-hour battle

limitations: Israel denied; no independent investigation found

title: Israeli letter S/8295 on Nuwaseirat tribe
claims_supported: Denied forced expulsion; said some crossed voluntarily after security restriction
limitations: State position; compare with Jordan claim

title: UN record of Jordan POW-treatment allegations and Israeli response
claims_supported: Jordan alleged torture, medical neglect and poor Atlit conditions; Israel denied and cited ICRC access
limitations: No independent finding in source

title: UN Yearbook account of deportation dispute over two Arab leaders
claims_supported: Jordan alleged two leaders deported for refusing cooperation; Israel cited security/welfare
limitations: Underlying letters need review

title: Yearbook of the United Nations 1968, Middle East chapter
claims_supported: February and March attacks on Karameh; Irbid and Salt attacks; Lebanon shelling claims; occupied-territory allegations, expulsions, decree, settlements; Beirut airport raid, Israel's acknowledgment and U.S. position; December Jordan incidents
limitations: Annual synthesis; attributes claims to states and summarizes UN records but not an independent incident investigation for every allegation

title: Jordan letter S/8391 on shelling of Karameh and nearby villages
claims_supported: Jordan reported 17 civilians killed and 60 wounded after Israeli shelling on 8 February
limitations: State complaint; figures not independently verified

title: Jordan letter S/8419 on attacks, displacement and expulsions
claims_supported: Jordan reported 16 civilians and 7 soldiers killed, 32 civilians and 27 soldiers injured, thousands displaced, and 84 West Bank residents expelled
limitations: State complaint; figures and 84-person expulsion claim not independently verified

title: Report of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA on the Exodus from the Jordan Valley, S/8435 (A/7060)
author_or_issuing_body: UNRWA Commissioner-General; transmitted by UN Secretary-General
claims_supported: UNRWA reported an exodus of about 5,000 civilians from the East Bank Jordan Valley after military incidents on 8 and 15 February
limitations: Figure is an approximate total for the cited exodus; may include Palestinians, refugees and other civilians; not a total for all 1968 displacement

title: Security Council Resolution 248 (1968) on Israeli military actions against Jordan
claims_supported: Observed Israeli action in Jordan was large-scale and carefully planned; condemned it as a flagrant violation of the Charter and cease-fire resolutions; deplored deaths and property damage
limitations: UN legal/political finding, not a criminal court judgment and no casualty total

title: Israeli Jets Knock Out Jordanian Artillery; Settlements Reported Extensively Damaged
claims_supported: Reports Jordan's complaint that Israeli rockets attacked Irbid and Israel's claim that it knocked out Jordanian artillery
limitations: Contemporary report relays competing claims; casualty details need UN documentary cross-check

title: Security Council Resolution 256 (1968) on Israeli military attacks against Jordan
claims_supported: Condemned further Israeli attacks as flagrant violations of Charter and Resolution 248, deplored loss of life/property damage, warned against repetition
limitations: Council resolution; does not give independently reconciled casualties

title: UN military observer report of investigation into Hula complaint, transmitted as S/8678
author_or_issuing_body: UN Israel-Lebanese Mixed Armistice Commission; Capt. J. Legrand
claims_supported: Observed 45 impact sites, shell fragments and damage; recorded death of Fatima Mohammed Ayoub and two wounded; found Hebrew-marked flare-shell components
limitations: One-sided investigation requested by Lebanon; no inquiry inside Israel and source attribution remained contested

title: Lebanon letter S/8583 and Israeli response S/8585 concerning Hula
claims_supported: Lebanon alleged Israeli shelling; Israel said it returned fire after Israeli villages had been shelled
limitations: Includes state positions; detailed inquiry is separately logged as UN68-HULA-INVESTIGATION

title: UNTSO inquiry documents S/7930/Add.107 and Add.108 on Beirut airport
claims_supported: Lebanese complaint reported 13 civilian aircraft destroyed; UN observers interviewed witnesses and saw 13 destroyed aircraft
limitations: Aircraft-count evidence; no casualties reported

title: Security Council Resolution 262 (1968) on Israeli military operations against Lebanon
claims_supported: Condemned Israel's premeditated action against Beirut civil airport as a Charter and cease-fire violation and recognized Lebanon's entitlement to redress
limitations: UN resolution, not a criminal court judgment

title: UN settlement chronology for West Bank and Jordan Valley
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Special Committee / Secretary-General report
claims_supported: Lists Jordan Valley settlements including Argaman, Kalia and Mehola as established in 1968
limitations: Retrospective inventory; some establishment dates vary across sources; land parcel impacts require independent records

title: UN settlement inventory in occupied Syrian Golan, S/1980/4
claims_supported: Lists Golan settlements including Ein Zivan and Mevo Hama founded in 1968 and identifies settlement relationships to former Syrian villages/land
limitations: Retrospective; does not quantify 1968 displacement by site

title: UN settlement inventory in occupied territories, S/1980/4
claims_supported: Lists Ramat Eshkol as a 1968 East Jerusalem settlement with 1,700 housing units and about 600 dunums of expropriated Arab land
limitations: Retrospective; not a household-level displacement record

title: UN Special Committee report A/8089 quoting ICRC Nablus and Hebron prison reports
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Special Committee, quoting International Committee of the Red Cross reports
source_type: UN human-rights report quoting institutional records
claims_supported: Nablus report of 26 February 1968 recorded torture allegations during military-police interrogation; Hebron report of 31 October 1968 described brutal treatment and named scarred prisoners
limitations: Later report quotes original ICRC reports, which were not directly reviewed; no count of affected detainees

title: UN Special Committee A/8089 summary of ICRC reporting on Golan displacement pressures
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Special Committee, quoting International Committee of the Red Cross
source_type: UN human-rights report quoting institutional records
claims_supported: Reports ICRC efforts to stop pressures that were forcing remaining residents to leave the occupied Golan; Israel stated the occupation forces were not making residents leave or stay
limitations: Retrospective summary; no verified annual displacement total

title: UN Yearbook 1968 record of UAR charge concerning Gaza population displacement
author_or_issuing_body: United Arab Republic claim summarized by United Nations
source_type: UN annual review of state complaint
claims_supported: UAR alleged 35,000 Gaza inhabitants were evicted during February; Israel denied the charge
limitations: Contested allegation; no verified count or independent inquiry identified

title: Yearbook of the United Nations 1969, Middle East section
claims_supported: UN summary of 1969 complaints and responses; Jordan's reported civilian casualties at Es-Salt; Lebanon allegations and 3 October kidnapping; treatment of civilian populations
limitations: Annual retrospective summarizes complaints and replies; not a complete incident register

title: Letter dated 26 March 1969 from Jordan to the President of the Security Council (S/9113)
author_or_issuing_body: Jordan, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Jordan alleged Israeli jet attack on villages and civilian centres near Es-Salt; reported 17 killed and 25 wounded
limitations: State complaint; Israel said it targeted a claimed Fatah base; casualty count not independently enumerated in the complaint

title: UNTSO report on inquiry into Israeli air attack on Hamah, 24 February 1969
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Truce Supervision Organization, summarized in UN Yearbook
claims_supported: Observers saw destroyed and damaged houses, factories and other buildings, and 31 hospitalized persons reported injured after Israeli air attack; Israel said attack targeted two Fatah bases in self-defence
limitations: Observer findings establish physical damage and hospitalized injured persons, but not their civilian/combatant status or the full casualty count

title: Letter dated 11 August 1969 from Lebanon to the President of the Security Council (S/9381)
author_or_issuing_body: Lebanon, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Lebanon alleged Israeli air attack on six southern villages using napalm, rockets and machine guns, killing four civilians and wounding three
limitations: Complaint attribution; exact victims not independently rostered in cited document

title: Security Council Resolution 270 (1969)
claims_supported: Council condemned the premeditated Israeli air attack on villages in southern Lebanon and deplored violent ceasefire violations and extension of fighting
limitations: Resolution condemns the attack; not a criminal court judgment or finding of individual criminal guilt

title: Letter dated 4 September 1969 from Lebanon to the President of the Security Council (S/9433)
author_or_issuing_body: Lebanon, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Lebanon alleged Israeli helicopters landed Israeli troops at Halta village; claimed one civilian killed and two wounded
limitations: State complaint; verify whether UNTSO inquiry exists before treating casualty attribution as established

title: Unrest Simmers in East Jerusalem, Occupied Areas; Troops Prevent Disorders
claims_supported: Israeli police sealed off Nablus old quarter amid demonstrations; reports police warning fire at Tulkarem; describes unrest in Gaza, Jerusalem and West Bank
limitations: Contemporaneous report; event detail and casualty totals limited

title: Dayan Visits West Bank Towns Troubled by Students and Business Shut-downs
claims_supported: Israeli police arrested nine Arab boys and eight girls in East Jerusalem; reports deportation of Nablus teacher Kassem Muhammed Hijjawi to Jordan
limitations: Contemporary report; says authorities accused teacher of funding non-cooperation; no legal file or detention record reviewed

title: Report of the Special Working Group of Experts on the Human Rights Situation in the Occupied Territories
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Commission on Human Rights Special Working Group
claims_supported: Report records allegations of beatings of 25 girls in Nablus and Jerusalem prisons in March 1969 and related allegations concerning detention and ill-treatment
limitations: The cited testimony was submitted by witnesses and advocacy sources; distinguish allegations from direct group findings and Israel's responses

title: Israeli settlements: Security Council Commission report under Resolution 465 (1980)
claims_supported: Inventory lists French Hill, Jerusalem, as established 1969 on Arab land and land from a Catholic convent
limitations: Retrospective inventory; supports recorded establishment year and land description but not exact 1969 land seizure date or acreage

title: Report of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA, 1 July 1968–30 June 1969
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees
claims_supported: Provides displacement context; says approximately 75,000 refugees had abandoned Jordan Valley camps in February–March 1968 and were in temporary camps in east Jordan
limitations: These are 1968 displaced people still receiving assistance during 1968–69, not a 1969 annual displacement count

title: Yearbook of the United Nations 1970, Middle East section
claims_supported: Chronology and UN proceedings concerning 1970 Israeli military actions in Lebanon, Jordan, and occupied Palestinian territory
limitations: Annual retrospective of complaints and UN actions; not comprehensive

title: Security Council Resolution 279 (1970)
claims_supported: Demanded immediate withdrawal of Israeli armed forces from Lebanese territory after the 12 May incursion
limitations: Requires reading alongside resolution text and surrounding Council record

title: Letter dated 22 May 1970 from Lebanon to the President of the Security Council (S/9811)
author_or_issuing_body: Lebanon, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Lebanon alleged Israeli artillery shelled four villages, reporting 20 killed, 40 wounded, and 150 homes destroyed or damaged
limitations: State complaint and preliminary casualty report; no independent victim roster cited

title: Security Council Resolution 280 (1970)
claims_supported: Council characterized Israeli military attack against Lebanon as premeditated, large-scale and carefully planned; repeated warning against armed attacks
limitations: Council resolution is not a criminal court judgment

title: Letter dated 5 June 1970 from Lebanon to the President of the Security Council (S/9822)
author_or_issuing_body: Lebanon, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Lebanon stated that 50,000 persons had been forced to seek refuge in other Lebanese regions following cumulative Israeli actions beginning 12 May

title: Secretary-General report on 5 September 1970 Lebanon incursion and resolution 285
source_type: UN report and Security Council proceedings
claims_supported: Lebanon reported two Israeli infantry companies penetrated seven kilometres and bombed civilian installations; Resolution 285 demanded complete and immediate withdrawal; Lebanon later reported withdrawal on 6 September, not directly observed by UN observers
limitations: Initial attack allegation not directly observed; withdrawal information relayed by Lebanese authorities

title: Letter dated 10 April 1970 from Jordan to the President of the Security Council (S/9764)
author_or_issuing_body: Jordan, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Jordan alleged repeated Israeli attacks on civilian centres, fields, factories, schools and a funeral procession from January through 10 April; reported more than 90 Jordanians killed or wounded, mostly civilians
limitations: State complaint aggregates multiple incidents; casualty roster and individual event totals not supplied

title: Letter dated 30 June 1970 from Jordan to the President of the Security Council (S/9852)
author_or_issuing_body: Jordan, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Jordan alleged Israeli jet aircraft attacked and strafed a civilian bus in northern Jordan Valley, killing two people and wounding 13
limitations: Casualty numbers and bus status attributed to Jordan's complaint; no independent roster located

title: Letter dated 18 August 1970 from Jordan to the President of the Security Council (S/9912)
author_or_issuing_body: Jordan, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Jordan reported over 100 Israeli attacks from 11 April to 28 July by shelling, bombing, strafing, infiltration and mining; alleged shelling of the Jordan Valley, Irbid and villages
limitations: Party complaint summarizes many events; exact casualty and displacement totals require event-specific follow-up

title: Report of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA, 1 July 1969–30 June 1970
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees
claims_supported: Reported Israeli military curfews, screenings, detention/deportation of UNRWA staff, two cases of six-month banishment to Sinai, Gaza shelter demolition and arrest of trainees inside Agency premises
limitations: Reporting period crosses two calendar years; no annual displaced-person total for 1970 follows from these operational data

title: Israeli settlements: list submitted to the Commission on Palestine
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People
claims_supported: Lists Mevo Horon, established in 1970, as a moshav in the Modi'in area
limitations: Retrospective inventory; does not identify exact land acquisition date or displacement count

title: Major Robert P. Perry, USA memorial entry
claims_supported: Identifies U.S. Army attaché Major Robert P. Perry as killed in Jordan on 10 June 1970 by Palestinian gunmen; contextual scope exclusion only
limitations: Not a record of an Israeli-perpetrated casualty and not included as an incident in this dataset

title: Yearbook of the United Nations 1971, Middle East section
claims_supported: Summary of complaints and responses on expulsions and occupied-territory policies; UNRWA special Gaza report and General Assembly Resolution 2792 C; Israel's stated rationale
limitations: Annual retrospective; incident details should be traced to the referenced original documents

title: Supplement to UNRWA special report on Gaza operations, A/8383/Add.1
author_or_issuing_body: UNRWA Commissioner-General, transmitted by UN Secretary-General
claims_supported: Confirms 14,704 persons affected in Jabalia, Beach and Rafah camps; 4,428 agency-built/assisted rooms and 2,000–3,000 privately built rooms demolished; reports displaced families' locations
limitations: Figures differ from later annual report; distinguish persons affected from people described as displaced

title: Report of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA, 1 July 1971–30 June 1972, paras. 14–15
claims_supported: Reports 7,729 rooms demolished and 15,855 persons displaced in Jabalia, Beach and Rafah camps during July–August 1971; records Israeli authorities' security rationale and UNRWA objection
limitations: Reporting is retrospective and gives a higher affected/displaced total than A/8383/Add.1; preserve discrepancy

title: General Assembly Resolution 2792 C (XXVI), Palestine refugees / UNRWA reports
claims_supported: Declared destruction of refugee shelters and forcible removal of occupants contravened Geneva Convention IV articles 49 and 53; called for halt, return and adequate shelter
limitations: General Assembly resolution; not a criminal court judgment

title: Dayan Visits Refugees Transferred from Gaza to Sinai
claims_supported: Reports Defense Minister Moshe Dayan visited El Arish housing prepared for families to be evacuated from Jabalia refugee camp
limitations: Brief wire report; does not give final total or document consent/return arrangements

title: Letter dated 26 March 1971 from Jordan to the President of the Security Council concerning expulsions
author_or_issuing_body: Jordan, transmitted to UN Security Council; summarized in UN Yearbook 1971
claims_supported: Jordan alleged 111 Arab inhabitants of Gaza and West Bank were forcibly expelled and deported to East Bank between 8 December 1970 and 24 February 1971; claimed inhuman conditions
limitations: State complaint covers two calendar years; preserve attribution and period

title: Letter dated 8 January 1971 from Jordan to the Secretary-General (A/8271)
author_or_issuing_body: Jordan, transmitted to the United Nations
claims_supported: Jordan alleged Israeli authorities deported 18 residents from the West Bank on 7 January 1971
limitations: State allegation; likely included in broader 111-person period count, so do not sum

title: Letter dated 15 January 1971 from Lebanon and Israel's reply on Sarafand (S/10078/S/10081)
author_or_issuing_body: Lebanon and Israel, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Lebanon said Israeli helicopter-borne force attacked Sarafand village north of the southern border; Israel said the action targeted a base used to launch raiders into Israel and cited a Fatah acknowledgment
limitations: Competing claims; no casualty count or independent site inquiry found in this record

title: Letter dated 16 June 1971 from Lebanon to the President of the Security Council (S/10226)
author_or_issuing_body: Lebanon, transmitted to UN Security Council
claims_supported: Lebanon listed ten Israeli actions from 3 May to 7 June: mortar shelling, incursions/fortification, fire at shepherds (one wounded), killing of one civilian at Ramya, and destruction of houses/car

title: Report of the Special Committee to Investigate Israeli Practices Affecting Human Rights in Occupied Territories (A/8389)
claims_supported: Records witness allegations of ill-treatment in interrogation at Sarafand, including detainees later deported in 1971; committee cited strong evidence in prior cases of regular ill-treatment in several prisons

title: Acquisition of land in Palestine: UN report on settlement establishment
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People
claims_supported: States seven new Israeli settlements were established in 1971
limitations: Retrospective compilation; not a record of every land acquisition or population affected

title: Israeli settlements in Gaza and the West Bank, Part II: establishment list
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Division for Palestinian Rights
claims_supported: Dates Mitzpe Shalem (Kibbutz, Jordan Valley/Dead Sea) to 1971
limitations: Retrospective list; no exact land acquisition date or displacement count

title: Yearbook of the United Nations 1971: land confiscation and Gaza resettlement plan allegation
source_type: UN annual review of state complaint
claims_supported: Records report that Israeli Military Governor informed village leaders north of Ramallah of intent to confiscate lands to resettle Gaza refugees
limitations: Reported prospective measure; does not establish whether confiscation or transfer occurred

title: Report of the Secretary-General on Palestine refugees in the Gaza Strip (A/8814)
claims_supported: Records Gaza demolitions began on 20 July and continued through 26 August 1971; UNRWA estimate of 2,554 families and 15,855 persons affected
limitations: Later report; its count differs from UNRWA November 1971 supplement A/8383/Add.1
